decisions.conflict: Glass-fiber reinforcement increases housing durability during the use phase but severely degrades the recyclability of the polymer at end-of-life.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (t), page 80: lightweight design as expressed through reduction of material consumption
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (h), page 79: use or content of recycled materials and recovery of materials
decisions.chief_resolution: Select unreinforced rPC/ABS blend with a minimum of 50% recycled content. This avoids composite materials that complicate recycling while maintaining sufficient impact resistance for a cordless screwdriver, aligning with the mandate to promote recycled content and material recovery.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of high-quality, UL-certified recycled PC/ABS resin suppliers in the EU market to verify compliance with safety standards before finalizing the material specification.

decisions.conflict: Ultrasonic welding minimizes assembly time and manufacturing costs but prevents non-destructive disassembly for repair or component recovery.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, including ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e), page 79: avoidance of technical solutions detrimental to reuse, upgrading, repair, maintenance, refurbishment, remanufacturing and recycling
decisions.chief_resolution: Specify standard threaded fasteners (screws) with brass inserts. This ensures non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly using commonly available tools, directly supporting the repairability and maintenance requirements of Annex I (b).
decisions.design_action: Verify the availability of standard metric screw sizes and corresponding brass inserts to minimize the variety of fasteners required for disassembly.

decisions.conflict: Brushed DC motors are cheaper and simpler to manufacture but suffer from lower energy efficiency and shorter technical lifetimes due to brush wear.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (g), page 79: use or consumption of energy, water and other resources during the product lifecycle
decisions.chief_resolution: Select a Brushless DC (BLDC) motor. Although it has a higher initial material footprint, its superior energy efficiency and lack of wearing brushes significantly extend the technical lifetime and reduce in-use energy consumption.
decisions.design_action: Check the supply chain for rare-earth magnet sourcing in the BLDC motor to evaluate the potential impact on critical raw material recovery.

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via optimized housing ventilation slots
Active cooling with an integrated plastic fan on the motor shaft
decisions.conflict: Phase change materials provide excellent thermal regulation but introduce complex chemical mixtures that complicate material recovery and recycling at end-of-life.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: resistance to stresses or ageing mechanisms
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e), page 79: avoidance of technical solutions detrimental to recycling of products and components
decisions.chief_resolution: Implement passive cooling via optimized housing ventilation slots combined with a lightweight, press-fitted fan on the motor shaft. This avoids the introduction of chemical substances of concern or complex material mixtures, facilitating clean material recovery.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the thermal thresholds of the selected battery cells and motor to establish the minimum passive airflow area required.

options_evaluated: Modular architecture with separate battery, motor, and gear modules
Semi-modular design with soldered wire connections
decisions.conflict: A monolithic chassis reduces assembly steps and part count but forces the replacement of the entire tool if a single component like the trigger switch fails.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance as expressed through modularity and standard components
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c), page 79: ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment
decisions.chief_resolution: Adopt a fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectors between the battery, motor/gearbox, and control PCB. This allows independent replacement of high-wear components, maximizing the product's technical lifetime and ease of repair.
decisions.design_action: Check the availability and reliability of standardized, lead-free board-to-board and wire-to-board connectors that can withstand tool vibration.

options_evaluated: Removable and standardized slide-on Lithium-Ion battery pack
Corded power supply with AC/DC converter
decisions.conflict: An integrated battery pack allows for a more compact and lightweight tool design but leads to premature product disposal when the battery cells inevitably degrade.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components as expressed through technical lifetime
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, including availability of spare parts
decisions.chief_resolution: Implement a removable, standardized slide-on battery pack. This ensures the battery can be easily replaced by the end-user when its capacity fades, preventing premature obsolescence of the entire screwdriver.
decisions.design_action: Investigate existing industry-standard battery interfaces (such as open battery alliances) to verify compatibility and potential for cross-brand interoperability.
